knowledge:
- key_parameters: species=Specifies the species of the input dataset (default is 'mouse', supports 'human' with gene mapping) ;; gname.type=The type of gene IDs used in the input dataset (e.g., 'ENSEMBL', 'SYMBOL') ;; ref.m=A custom reference projection matrix (defaults to the pre-learned mouse Neurosphere reference) ;; dimred=The name of the reduced dimension slot to store or retrieve the embedding (defaults to 'tricycleEmbedding') ;; bw=The bandwidth/concentration parameter of the von Mises distribution used in kernel density estimation (e.g., set to 10 for smooth lines on small datasets) ;; type=The type of plot for kernel density estimation, either 'circular' (polar coordinates) or 'linear' (Cartesian coordinates) ;; exprs_values=The assay slot containing normalized expression values (defaults to 'logcounts')
- alternatives: estimate_Schwabe_stage=An alternative discrete cell cycle stage predictor (predicting 5 stages) based on a modification of Schwabe et al. (2020) / Revelio package, provided for convenience but not part of the core tricycle method ;; CircStats::circ.cor=Used instead of traditional Pearson's correlation coefficient to calculate the correlation between two cyclic variables (like cell cycle positions) without ignoring their cyclic nature
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing single-cell RNA-seq data (human or mouse, across various technologies like 10X or Fluidigm C1) and wanting to infer a continuous, high-resolution relative time/position within the cell cycle rather than discrete stages.
- pitfalls: Users must normalize library size (e.g., using scater::normalizeCounts or calculating CPM) before putting data into tricycle functions ;; The absence of an empty interior in the ellipsoid projection plot does not mean the method failed; it is often just a consequence of lower sequencing depth ;; Traditional Pearson's correlation coefficient fails to account for the cyclic nature of cell cycle positions (0 and 2pi are adjacent); circular correlation (CircStats::circ.cor) must be used instead ;; Re-learning a reference via PCA can result in flipped signs for PC1/PC2 (causing a pi shift), so circular correlation is still necessary to compare positions.

workflows.name: cell_cycle_inference_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Project single-cell RNA-seq data into the pre-learned cell cycle space, estimate continuous cell cycle positions, and visualize the results.
workflows.stages: 1. Project data into the pre-learned cell cycle space using project_cycle_space() ;; 2. Estimate continuous cell cycle position using estimate_cycle_position() ;; 3. Fit periodic loess to key marker genes using fit_periodic_loess() ;; 4. Plot kernel density of cell cycle positions using plot_ccposition_den() ;; 5. Plot embedding colored by cell cycle position using plot_emb_circle_scale() and circle_scale_legend()
workflows.code:
neurosphere_example <- project_cycle_space(neurosphere_example)
neurosphere_example <- estimate_cycle_position(neurosphere_example)
top2a.idx <- which(rowData(neurosphere_example)$Gene == 'Top2a')
fit.l <- fit_periodic_loess(neurosphere_example$tricyclePosition,
                            assay(neurosphere_example, 'logcounts')[top2a.idx,],
                            plot = TRUE,
                       x_lab = "Cell cycle position \u03b8", y_lab = "log2(Top2a)",
                       fig.title = paste0("Expression of Top2a along \u03b8 (n=",
                                          ncol(neurosphere_example), ")"))
fit.l$fig + theme_bw(base_size = 14)
plot_ccposition_den(neurosphere_example$tricyclePosition,
                    neurosphere_example$sample, 'sample',
                    bw = 10, fig.title = "Kernel density of \u03b8") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)

plot_ccposition_den(neurosphere_example$tricyclePosition,
                    neurosphere_example$sample, 'sample', type = "circular",
                    bw = 10,  fig.title = "Kernel density of \u03b8") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
p <- plot_emb_circle_scale(neurosphere_example, dimred = 1,
                           point.size = 3.5, point.alpha = 0.9) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
legend <- circle_scale_legend(text.size = 5, alpha = 0.9)
plot_grid(p, legend, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(1, 0.4))

workflows.name: discrete_stage_inference
workflows.intent: Infer discrete cell cycle stages (G1/S, S, G2, G2/M, M/G1) using the Schwabe et al. (2020) method.
workflows.stages: 1. Estimate discrete cell cycle stages using estimate_Schwabe_stage() ;; 2. Plot the projected cell cycle space colored by the predicted stages
workflows.code:
neurosphere_example <- estimate_Schwabe_stage(neurosphere_example,
                                            gname.type = 'ENSEMBL',
                                            species = 'mouse')
scater::plotReducedDim(neurosphere_example, dimred = "tricycleEmbedding",
                       colour_by = "CCStage") +
  labs(x = "Projected PC1", y = "Projected PC2",
       title = paste0("Projected cell cycle space (n=", ncol(neurosphere_example), ")")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)

workflows.name: custom_reference_projection
workflows.intent: Build a custom cell cycle reference using PCA on Gene Ontology cell cycle genes and project data using this new reference.
workflows.stages: 1. Run PCA on Gene Ontology cell cycle genes using run_pca_cc_genes() ;; 2. Extract the rotation matrix for the top 2 PCs to serve as the new reference ;; 3. Estimate cell cycle position using the custom reference matrix with estimate_cycle_position() ;; 4. Compare the new positions with original positions using circular correlation
workflows.code:
set.seed(100)
gocc_sce.o <- run_pca_cc_genes(neurosphere_example,
                               exprs_values = "logcounts", species = "mouse")
new.ref <- attr(reducedDim(gocc_sce.o, 'PCA'), 'rotation')[, seq_len(2)]
head(new.ref)
new_sce <- estimate_cycle_position(neurosphere_example, ref.m  = new.ref,
                                   dimred = 'tricycleEmbedding2')
cor(neurosphere_example$tricyclePosition, new_sce$tricyclePosition)
CircStats::circ.cor(neurosphere_example$tricyclePosition, new_sce$tricyclePosition)
qplot(x = neurosphere_example$tricyclePosition,y = new_sce$tricyclePosition) +
  labs(x = "Original \u03b8", y = "New \u03b8",
       title = paste0("Comparison of two \u03b8 (n=", ncol(neurosphere_example), ")")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
